author: Laboratoire d'InfoRmatique en Image et Systèmes d'information

description.en: PIIRRITE (Pedestrian InclusIve indooR-outdooR ITinerariEs) is an ontology for inclusive pedestrian navigation. It relies on GeoSPARQL, SAREF, OWL-Time, SKOS, etc. It is developed using the SAMOD methodology through successive modelets driven by a set of competency questions reflecting user requirements.
description.fr: PIIRRITE (Pedestrion InclusIve indooR-outdooR ITinerariEs) est une ontologie pour la navigation piétonne inclusive. Elle repose sur GeoSPARQL, SAREF, OWL-TIME, SKOS, etc. Elle est développée en utilisant la méthodologie SAMOD à travers des modelets successifs dirigés par un ensembe de questions de compétences qui reflètent des exigences utilisateurs.

V4.1.1: Introduced class saref:DeviceKind

comment.en: Device kinds allow to describe kinds of devices, with common properties and common states having the same value, targeting the same properties and states, common functions, and common services. Devices kinds may be used to describe models of devices in online catalogues.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Simplified definition and axiomatization of saref:Function. Added examples.

example.value: To accomplish the task of sensing the temperature, a temperature sensor should have a sensing function.
To accomplish the task of controlling the light, a smart light switch may have a function for turning on and off the light, and another to set the luminosity of the light.
To accomplish the task of washing clothes, a washing machine should have a function for washing.

comment.en: Logical groups of commands that devices support to accomplish their tasks. Function can target (OP saref:targets and its sub-properties) features, properties, or states. An instance of saref:Function can apply to different devices.

description.en: A LineString is a Curve with linear interpolation between Points. Each consecutive pair of Points defines a Line segment.

definition.value: An ordered collection of concepts, where both the grouping and the ordering are meaningful.

scopeNote.value: Ordered collections can be used where you would like a set of concepts to be displayed in a specific order, and optionally under a 'node label'.

comment.en: A polyline of interest that can be traveled through
comment.fr: Une polyligne d'intérêt dont le parcours est possible

note.value: Functions of interest need not always be explicited. It depends on the use case. Typically, functions of interest are useful to specify which command is actually exposed, and which actual property of interest or state of interest it targets.
A function of interest is the function of (OP saref:isFunctionOfInterestOf) exactly one device.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:FunctionOfInterest, parallel to saref:PropertyOfInterest.

comment.en: Logical groups of commands that devices support to accomplish their tasks. Function can target (OP saref:targets and its sub-properties) features, properties, or states. An instance of saref:FunctionOfInterest is supported by exactly one device.
A sequence of 1 or more consecutive segments located in a geographic space and contextualised by properties
comment.fr: Une séquence d'1 ou plus segments consécutifs localisée dans un espace géographique et contextualisée par des propriétés

comment.en: A condition that a spatial element should meet in order to be considered valid.
comment.fr: Une condition qu'un élément spatial doit respecter pour être considéré valide.

comment.en: A distance factor for the corresponding condition to be considered respected.
comment.fr: Un facteur de distance pour que la condition correspondante soit considérée respectée.

comment.en: A saref:Observation is the act of carrying out a procedure to estimate or calculate a value of a property of a feature of interest, or a state of a feature of interest. It links to a sensor to describe what made the observation, and to the observed feature, property, property of interest, state, or state of interest. Typically, its result is a property value or a state. An observation of a state (OP saref:observes) should have a state as a result (OP saref:hasResult). Respectively, an observation of a property should have a property value as a result.
A value wrapper representing the importance of a requirement using a float between 0 and 1. The importance can also be equal to INF if the requirement is mandatory.
comment.fr: Une enveloppe de valeur décrivant l'importance d'une exigence par un réel entre 0 et 1. L'importance peut également valoir INF si le besoin doit obligatoirement être respecté lors de la génération d'itinéraires.

note.value: Tasks can be accomplished by devices (saref:isAccomplishedBy).

example.value: For example, a washing machine is designed for the task of washing.

comment.en: The goal for which a device is designed, from a user perspective.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:PropertyValue to simplify the association of a measure to a property, without always needing it to be a measurement made by a device.
V4.1.1: saref:hasValue is now optional on saref:PropertyValue.

comment.en: Describes the value for a property. The property value is optionally linked to its value expressed as an RDF literal (DP saref:hasValue), optionally to the unit of measurement (OP saref:isMeasuredIn), and optionally to the properties or properties of interest it is a value of (OP saref:isValueOfProperty).

description.en:
A Point is a 0-dimensional geometric object and represents a single location in coordinate space. 
A Point has an x-coordinate value, a y-coordinate value. If called for by the associated Spatial Reference System, it may also have coordinate values for z and m.
The boundary of a Point is the empty set.

note.value: The applicable context can be restricted to when a feature of interest has a certain state (OPs saref:whenState).
OP saref:hasPrice links a profile to the money earned (negative values) or paid (positive values) for the use (production or consumption) of the commodity by the device.
The applicable context can be restricted to when the property of a feature of interest has some value (OPs saref:whenPropertyValue)

The applicable context of a profile can be bound temporally using DP saref:hasTimestamp or its subproperties defined by SAREF extensions, or OP saref:hasApplicableTime which links to instant or interval or other compound temporal entity expressed using OWL Time.

OP saref:hasProfile links a device to its profile. The device should be linked to a certain commodity using OP saref:consumes, saref:produces, or saref:stores, and optionally to some property or state using OP saref:targets or its sub-properties.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Class saref:Profile has been re-specified, to take into account findings from SAREF4ENER V1.2.1.

comment.en: A saref:Profile describes the money earned (negative values) or paied (positive values) for the use (production or consumption) of a commodity by a device in a certain context.
A user profile, described by a set of requirement (eg. 'I want to use elevators') rather than by personnal characteristics (eg. I'm in a wheelchair).
comment.fr: Le profil d'un utilisateur, décrit par un ensemble d'exigences (eg. 'Je veux prendre l'ascenseur') plutôt que par des caractéristiques personnels (eg. 'Je suis en fauteuil').

comment.en: A dimensionless entity located in a geographic space and contextualised by properties
comment.fr: Une entité sans dimension localisée dans un espace géographique et contextualisée par des propriétés

note.value: Concepts from existing code lists, vocabularies, and taxonomies, may be used as instances of saref:Property.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: The definition and scope of usage for saref:Property is clarified. Axiomatization is simplified.

Until SAREF V3.1.1, there was an ambiguity between whether properties should be specific or generic to features of interest. This ambiguity has been solved in SAREF V3.2.1, and the new modeling will be enforced in the next major revision of SAREF.

example.value: Air temperature, pressure, luminance, etc. are all properties.

comment.en: Identifiable qualities of features of interest that can be target of devices, such as observed or controlled. A property can apply to different features of interest.
An operator usable for combining conditions into a composed validity expression.
comment.fr: Un opérateur utilisable pour combiner des conditions en une expression de validité composée.

note.value: SAREF refers to energy commodities such as electricity, gas, coal and oil.

Concepts from existing code lists, vocabularies, and taxonomies, may be used as instances of saref:Commodity, for example from the ISDA taxonomy of commodities, the Standard International Energy product Classification (SIEC), the IRENA Energy Taxonomy or Wikidata.

historyNote.value: V4.1.1: Removed examples of commodity categories.
V3.2.1: Definition of saref:Commodity is simplified.

comment.en: A marketable item which may be supplied without qualitative differentiation.
A 2D area over a geographic space represented as a polygon and contextualised by properties which are inherited by all context-faring entities contained within the area
comment.fr: Une région 2D d'un espace géographique représentée par un polygon et contextualisée par des propriétés qui sont hérités par toutes les entitées porteuses de contexte contenues dans la région

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:ProcedureExecution.

comment.en: Represents the act of carrying out a procedure.

note.value: States of interest need not always be explicited. It depends on the use case. Typically, states of interest are useful in applications, where the association between a feature of interest and a state (i.e., the state of interest) needs to be identified and related to other states of interest.
Per convention, the IRI of states of interest should consist of the IRI of their feature of interest, suffixed with a fragment identifier #{S} where {S} refers to the name of the state.
A state of interest is the state of (OP saref:isStateOfInterestOf) exactly one feature of interest.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:StateOfInterest, parallel to saref:PropertyOfInterest.

comment.en: Identifiable conditions that features of interest are or may be in, and that can be target of devices, such as observed and controlled. An instance of saref:StateOfInterest is specific to a feature of interest. It is inherent to and cannot exist without that feature of interest.
A value wrapper representing the flexilibty of a requirement using a float between 0 and 1.
comment.fr: Une enveloppe de valeur décrivant la flexibilité d'une exigence par un réel entre 0 et 1.

comment.en: A condition composed of a logical operator and one or two operands that are themselves conditions.
comment.fr: Une condition composée d'un opérateur logique et d'un ou deux opérande étant eux-mêmes des conditions.

comment.en: A user requirement, represented by its importance, its rigor and one or many validity conditions
comment.fr: Une exigence d'un utilisateur, représentée par son importance, sa rigueur et une ou plusieurs conditions de validité.

comment.en: A saref:Actuation is the act of carrying out a procedure to control the state of the world using an actuator. It links to an actuator to describe what made the actuation, and to the controlled feature, property, property of interest, state, or state of interest. Typically, its input is a property value or a state. An actuation of a state (OP saref:controls) should have a state as input (OP saref:hasInput). Respectively, an actuation of a property should have a property value as input.

description.en: A discrete spatial phenomenon in a universe of discourse.

definition.value:
This class represents the top-level feature type. This class is

comment.en:

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Simplified definition and axiomatization of saref:Command. Added examples.

example.value: Observe property, control property, observe state, control state, invoke action, cancel action, turn on or off, change color, subscribe, publish, etc. are all commands.

comment.en: The lowest-level directives a function exposes to some network. Commands can target (OP saref:targets and its sub-properties) features, properties, or states. An instance of saref:Command is independent of any device.

description.undefined: VAEM Governed Object class is a placeholder for concepts that are fully defined by the voag:GovernedObject concept hierarchy for building a catalog of ontologies and graphs

definition.value: A set of concepts, optionally including statements about semantic relationships between those concepts.

example.value: Thesauri, classification schemes, subject heading lists, taxonomies, 'folksonomies', and other types of controlled vocabulary are all examples of concept schemes. Concept schemes are also embedded in glossaries and terminologies.

scopeNote.value: A concept scheme may be defined to include concepts from different sources.

note.value: Our definition is based on the definition of unit of measure in the Ontology of units of Measure (OM).
Concepts from existing code lists, vocabularies, and taxonomies, may be used as instances of saref:UnitOfMeasure. For example the QUDT Unit vocabulary

example.value: For example, consumption power is a property and Watt is a unit of power that represents a definite predetermined power: when we say 10 Watt, we actually mean 10 times the definite predetermined power "Watt".

comment.en: The unit of measure is a standard for measurement of a quantity, such as a Property.
A comparison or logical operator.
comment.fr: Un opérateur logique ou de comparaison.

note.value: Like for commands, commands of interest may be described in terms of their input parameters, outputs, and which properties or states they target.

Commands of interest need not always be explicited. It depends on the use case. Typically, commands of interest are useful to specify the actual property of interest or state of interest that is expected as input parameter, output, or that will be targeted.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:CommandOfInterest, parallel to saref:PropertyOfInterest.

example.value: The corridor smart light switch supports a command of kind “turn on/off”, which controls the state of the outdoor light.
The smart fridge supports a command of kind “observe temperature”, which observes the temperature of the fridge.

comment.en: The lowest-level directives a device supports and exposes to some network. Commands can target (OP saref:targets and its sub-properties) features, properties, or states. A saref:CommandOfInterest is a directives actually supported by a device and exposed to some network.

historyNote.value: V4.1.1: Definition of Sensor and Meter are updated to better distinguish one from the other.
V3.2.1: Definition of Sensor is simplified and grounded on saref:observes. Local restriction on saref:hasFunction is deleted.

comment.en: A device designed to observe and measure one or more properties or states of one or more features of interest.

note.value: SAREF is not restricted to binary states such as the ex:OnOffState, but allows to define also enumerated states.
Concepts from existing code lists, vocabularies, and taxonomies, may be used as instances of saref:State.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Clarified and generalized definition of saref:State. Can now apply to all features of interest, not just devices.

example.value: A switch can be found in the saref:OnOffState.

comment.en: Identifiable conditions that features of interest are or may be in, and that can be target of devices, such as observed and controlled. A state can apply to different features of interest.

definition.value: An idea or notion; a unit of thought.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Definition of saref:Appliance is grounded on tasks and commodities.

comment.en: A device designed to accomplish a particular task for occupant use. It consumes, produces, or stores, some commodity.

Describes the execution of an operation in a network: the–machine interpretable–  description of a communication between devices over the network. Typically, its input and result are network messages, that conform to the input and output of the executed operation.
An operator usable for the matching between a validity condition and the value of a contextual property. e.g. equality, membership, difference, superiority, etc.
comment.fr: Un opérateur utilisable lors du matching entre une condition de validité et une valeur de propriété contextuelle. e.g. égalité, appartenance, différence, supériorité, etc.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Definition of Actuator is simplified and grounded on saref:controls. Local restriction on saref:hasFunction is deleted.

comment.en: A device designed to control one or more properties or states of one or more features of interest.

historyNote.value: V4.1.1: Definition of Sensor and Meter are updated to better distinguish one from the other.
V3.2.1: Definition of Meter is simplified and grounded on saref:observes. Local restriction on saref:hasFunction is deleted.

comment.en: A device designed to observe and additionally do some computation and/or display one or more properties of one or more features of interest.

note.value: An operation may be described in terms of its inputs and outputs using OP saref:hasInput and saref:hasOutput. Inputs and outputs of operations typically describe the expected schema or shape of network messages.

Typically, a device connected to a given network offers one service for each of its functions of interest, and each service has one operation per command of interest of the function of interest it represents.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:Operation and associated properties from oneM2M base ontology.

example.value: In the set of operations exposed by a smart light bulb on a given network, one may be dedicated to turn on and off the light and expect a boolean as input. Another one may be dedicated to set the luminosity status and expect a target luminosity level (a byte) and a transition time (encoded on two bytes).

In the set of operations exposed by a smart washing machine on a given network, one may be dedicated to set the water temperature for the washing cycle, and expected as input a enumerated value. Another one may be dedicated to start, pause, or stop the washing cycle.
To turn on a light, send a CoAP PUT request with CBOR content 0xf5 (true)

comment.en: A saref:Operation is the means of a service to communicate in a procedure-type manner over the network (i.e. transmit data to/from other devices). It is the –machine interpretable– exposure of a –human understandable– command to a network.
A condition that a spatial element should meet in order to be considered valid from the corresponding property standpoint.
comment.fr: Une condition qu'un élément spatial doit respecter pour être considéré valide du point de vue de la propriété correspondante.

note.value: Per convention, the IRI of properties of interest should consist of the IRI of their feature of interest, suffixed with a fragment identifier #{P} where {P} refers to the name of the property.

Properties of interest need not always be explicited. It depends on the use case. Typically, properties of interest are useful in applications, where the association between a feature of interest and a property (i.e., the property of interest) needs to be identified and related to other properties of interest.
A property of interest is the property of (OP saref:isPropertyOfInterestOf) exactly one feature of interest.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:PropertyOfInterest to solved the ambiguity between generic vs specific properties.

comment.en: Identifiable qualities of features of interest that can be target of devices, such as observed or controlled. An instance of saref:PropertyOfInterest is specific to a feature of interest. It is inherent to and cannot exist without that feature of interest.

description.en: A coherent set of direct positions in Euclidian space. A direct position holds the coordinates for a position within a Coordinate Reference System (CRS).

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Simplified definition of saref:Service. Added examples.

example.value: For example, a light switch can offer the service of remotely switching the lights in a home through mobile phone devices that are connected to the local network (ex:SwitchOnService class). This "remote switching" service represents the ex:OnOffFunction.

comment.en: A saref:Service is a digital representation of a function in a network, making it discoverable, registerable and remotely controllable in the network.

Describes the execution of a command. Typically, its inputs and outputs are human understandable and relate to some feature of interest, such as its state (e.g., s4abcd:On), or the value of its temperature (e.g., property value 21.0 °C).

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Definition of saref:FeatureOfInterest: Clarify it's a specific real world entity.
V3.2.1: Definition of saref:FeatureOfInterest: allValuesFrom axioms are unnecessary and have been deleted.
V3.2.1: Definition of saref:FeatureOfInterest is clarified, not only properties are measured, but properties and states can be observed and controlled.

comment.en: A feature of interest represents any real world entity from which a property or a state may be targeted, such as observed and controlled. An instance of saref:FeatureOfInterest represents one specific real world entity.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: Introduced class saref:FeatureKind
V3.2.1: Use SKOS to organize generic classes in taxonomies.

comment.en: Feature kinds allow to describe kinds of features of interest, with common properties having the same value, and common states being the same. An instance of saref:FeatureKind represents an archetype of real world entities, for example to populate product catalogs.

historyNote.value: V3.2.1: saref:Device is explicitly a subclass of saref:FeatureOfInterest and s4syst:System.
V3.2.1: Most axioms on saref:Device were useless and have been deleted.
V3.2.1: definition of saref:Device clarifies it's a real world entity.

example.value: Examples of devices are a light switch, a temperature sensor, an energy meter, a water flow meter, and a laundry dryer. A laundry dryer is designed to dry laundry, and to accomplish this task it has a start/stop function.
For example, a washing machine is designed to wash (task) and to accomplish this task it performs a start and stop function.

comment.en: A tangible object designed to accomplish a particular task. In order to accomplish this task, the device performs one or more functions. An instance of saref:Device represents one specific real world entity.

definition.value: Links a concept to a concept related by meaning.
